mathgap.title: Signed 'has N more than'
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X has N more than Y", interpret it as X = Y + N (add N to Y). This preserves the direction of the "more than" relation.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement directly includes the phrase "has N more than" with a numeric N.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "Alice has 5 more than Bob" as "Bob = Alice + 5" (reversing the relation).

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: For a transfer "X gives N to Y", subtract N from X's count and add N to Y's count, updating the current counts accordingly.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a transfer of items from one person to another.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "Alice gives 3 to Bob" as adding 3 to Alice and subtracting 3 from Bob.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a variable for each person, translate every relevant statement into a linear equation (or inequality), and solve the resulting system algebraically.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After parsing all statements, before attempting to guess values.
mathgap.example: Guessing Alice's count without setting up equations, leading to contradictory results.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "the number of X increases by k times", treat it as multiplying the original amount by k (new = original * k).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering phrases like "increases by 9/5 times" or "increased by 24/11 times".
mathgap.example: Interpreting "increases by 9/5 times" as new = original + (9/5)*original instead of new = original * (9/5).

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the splitter's count to zero and add an equal share of the original amount to each recipient.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering statements like "X splits all their items equally among Y and Z."
mathgap.example: Forgetting to set the splitter's count to zero after splitting, leaving the original amount unchanged.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: When a statement uses the phrase "difference between X and Y" without qualifiers, treat it as the signed difference X - Y (preserving order), not the absolute difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement mentions "difference between X and Y".
mathgap.example: Interpreting "difference between A and B" as |A - B| instead of A - B.

mathgap.title: Sequential statement processing
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the order given, updating counts as you go; direct count statements set the current count at that point, and subsequent transfers or relational statements refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem includes a sequence of statements that may affect each other's values.
mathgap.example: Ignoring the order and treating all statements as simultaneous, causing inconsistent equations.

mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' in relational equations
mathgap.principle: In relational statements without a numeric amount, such as "the number of X that Y has more than Z", interpret "has more than" as a signed difference Y - Z, preserving the order.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational statement uses "has more than" but does not specify a numeric difference.
mathgap.example: Treating "the number of X that Y has more than Z" as an absolute difference instead of Y - Z.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Incorporate all transfer statements as equations linking the giver's and receiver's counts before using relational equations; this ensures the correct final counts are used in relational reasoning.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After parsing all transfer statements and before solving relational equations.
mathgap.example: Ignoring transfer constraints when solving relational equations, leading to inconsistent solutions.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: When a problem includes both direct count statements (e.g., "X has N items") and transfer statements, interpret the direct counts as describing the initial amounts before any transfers, unless the text explicitly indicates otherwise.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever direct count statements appear together with transfer statements.
mathgap.example: Assuming "Alice has 10 tomatoes" is the final amount after transfers, then also applying "Alice gives 3 to Bob", which leads to an impossible count for Alice.

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that direct counts are final, especially when transfers are also present, causing a mismatch in the system of equations.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as initial amounts before transfers, unless explicitly stated otherwise; apply transfers to update counts accordingly.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat a split as a simple addition to recipients without removing the original amount.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a person splits all their items equally, set their count to zero and give each recipient an equal share of the original amount.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: Misreading the phrase "X gives N to Y" as "X receives N from Y".
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Subtract N from the giver's count and add N to the receiver's count.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has more than' in relational equations as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to absolute difference when the phrase is ambiguous.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat "has more than" as a signed difference (X - Y).

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'difference between X and Y' as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase "difference between" is often interpreted as absolute difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order and treat it as a signed difference (X - Y).
